A. The responsibilities of the Equipment & Uniform Committee shall be to consider any changes in the uniform and personal equipment worn by commissioned personnel and make recommendations to the Chief of Police relative to:
p
1. New uniform and police equipment on the market.
p
2. Analyze and evaluate present uniform and personal equipment needs.
p
3. Investigate and report any problems with the quality of equipment or uniform materials.
p
4. Review bid specifications on police equipment and recommend department action.
p
5. Maintain a current roster of authorized equipment and uniform dealers.
p
6. Maintain all correspondence regarding uniform and equipment dealers.
p

B. Each member shall serve for a one (1) year tenure, except for the chairperson. The designated chairperson shall be the Training Division Captain and shall maintain a permanent authorized position. The chairperson shall not have voting privileges except when committee votes end in a tie and then the chairperson will vote to break the tie.
p

C. The committee shall consist of commissioned personnel desiring to serve an appointment as volunteers. Personnel serving on the committee shall vary depending upon each individual’s expertise to effectively evaluate equipment and uniform materials.
p

D. During the first quarter of each calendar year, the Training Division Captain shall solicit interest from officers in serving on the committee. Current members may request to be considered to serve another term. The chairperson will gather all letters of interest and forward, along with any recommendations, through the chain of command. The Chief of Police or designee shall approve all final appointments of committee members. E The committee shall be comprised of no more than fourteen (14) members. The goal is for committee members to represent the different assignments in the department. The committee shall include:
pre

1 Captain              Chairperson       Police Training Division
2 Lieutenants                            from a uniformed assignment
Up to 2 officers, any rank               from Investigative & Support Command
Up to 2 officers, any rank               from Tactical Command
Up to 3 officers, any rank               from North Command
Up to 3 officers, any rank               from South Command
1 Officer, any rank                      from the Police Officers’ Association Board
p

F. No officer shall wear a uniform item or any equipment item for testing purposes without first seeking approval from the Operational Command Deputy Chief. The Deputy Chief will coordinate with the Training Division Captain to determine items suitable for testing and evaluation. All items and personnel selected for testing will be documented by the Training Division Captain and suitability for permanent use will be determined by the Chief of Police or their designee.
p

G. All equipment and uniform reviews, complaints, evaluations, and other pertinent data shall be gathered and presented by the committee chairperson. The information shall, along with committee recommendations, be forwarded through the chain of command for review by the Chief of Police or designee. The Training Division Captain shall make the necessary notifications of any approved item(s) to the affected parties and, when appropriate, to Policy Management for any General Order revision.
p

H. The Operational Command shall serve as an advisory and information center to the committee on appropriate items being addressed. A catalog of items shall be created detailing items reviewed or acted upon in the past.
p

I. Committee meetings shall be held quarterly and minutes of the meetings shall be maintained by the Training Division Captain. The Training Division Captain may cancel quarterly meetings if there is no agenda to discuss or call more frequent meetings if circumstances warrant.
p

J. The first hour of the scheduled meeting session shall be utilized to receive officer suggestions and to allow comments about equipment problems that have been personally experienced. All of the comments shall be taken under advisement and answers shall be provided during the next scheduled meeting.
p
A. The responsibilities of the Fleet and Equipment Advisory Committee shall be to research and review proposed equipment and make recommendations relative to:
p
1. Review of new police equipment on the market, other than personal equipment reserved for review by the uniform committee,
p
2. Analysis and evaluation of present equipment needs, other than furniture or office fixtures,
p
3. Investigation and reports of any problems with the quality of equipment,
p
4. Review of bid specifications on police equipment and recommended department action, and
p
5. Approval and prioritization of all requests that involve vehicle or equipment purchases that:
p
a. Are expected to be classified as a capital expense exceeding $5,000 acquisition cost,
p
b. Must be registered with the Texas Department of Transportation,
p
c. Have a fuel capacity in excess of five (5) U.S. gallons, and/or
p
d. Require maintenance and/or repair by the Property Management Department’s Fleet Division.
p

B. The Budget and Finance Section’s Budget Committee shall promptly forward all vehicle and equipment needs request meeting the above criteria to the Fleet and Equipment Advisory Committee Chair for review.
p

C. The Fleet and Equipment Advisory Committee shall complete the review process prior to the end of the second quarter of the fiscal year for items that are to be included for the subsequent budget year. During the review, the Fleet and Equipment Advisory Committee shall consider the justification for the request, how the purchase of the requested vehicles or equipment contributes to the goals and objectives of the department, and make a final recommendation that is based on available resources and operational benefit to the department.
p

D. Each member shall serve for one (1) year tenure, except for the chairperson. The designated chairperson shall be the Manager of the Police Fleet/Auto Pound Division and shall maintain a permanent authorized position.
p

E. The committee shall consist of commissioned personnel desiring to serve an appointment as a volunteer. Qualifications of the personnel serving on the committee shall vary depending upon each individual’s expertise to effectively evaluate equipment. Committee members shall serve as a liaison to employees regarding equipment issues.
p
F. The Deputy Chief over the Fleet/Auto Pound Division shall approve all final appointments of committee members. The committee shall be comprised of the following eleven (11) members:
pre

Chairperson                          Public Safety Support Manager
Administrative Sergeant              Operational Command
3 appointed officers,                North Command
3 appointed officers,                South Command, including the Traffic Division
1 appointed officer, any rank        Tactical Command
1 officer, any rank                  Investigative & Support Command
1 officer, any rank                  Police Officers’ Association Board
p

G. All equipment reviews, complaints, evaluations, and other pertinent data shall be gathered and presented by the committee chairperson for review by the Deputy Chief over the Fleet/Auto Pound Division. The Deputy Chief will then forward relevant information to the Assistant Chief. Complaints pertaining to current equipment will be maintained by the committee chairperson in the files on vendors, solicitations, and awards.
p

H. Committee meetings shall be held quarterly, if determined appropriate by the Chairperson, at a designated location and minutes shall be maintained by the Finance and Personnel Bureau Administrative Sergeant. The date, time, and location of the meetings will be posted no less than ten (10) days before the planned meeting. These dates and times may be changed due to holidays or conflicts in scheduling.
